comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — hornet.com/tr still shows a full-screen first-party cookie-consent modal under the AdGuard baseline (the site's own localStorage consent flag is unset), so I propose hiding that modal with one domain-scoped Extended-CSS rule anchored on the consent form's own field name; apply_rule verified the symptom resolved with page integrity intact. ## Rule `hornet.com#?#.modal-portal:has(input[name="enablePersonalizedAds"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice, handled by the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter family; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close/hand-off rules applies. No anti-adblock detector or wall is involved:⁠ the page renders its content behind the overlay and no detector script appears in the captured requests. The existing per-site rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt show this repository fixes this site's cookie annoyance with filter rules. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 2176](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L2176). ## Missing information - Scriptlet argument syntax for values containing commas (set-local-storage-item with a JSON value): The linked syntax document's "Scriptlet rules" section only states that arguments are "a list of string arguments" and shows examples with single simple values; it does not say how a scriptlet argument that itself contains commas (for example a JSON string such as {"is_set":⁠true,"ads":⁠false}) must be written or escaped, nor whether AdGuard's rule parser splits such an argument into several arguments. I need this to decide whether hornet.com's consent state can be set with #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('set-local-storage-item', 'consent', '<⁠json⁠>') or whether only a comma-free value/selector-based approach is viable. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"1805ccf5e25cfa555d5e5a960478b04a64773f9950ef25ac232f2f31f8f3e371"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — jpopsingles.eu serves an inline "AdBlock Detected" detector that builds a randomized-id full-screen overlay, locks scrolling and breaks right-click, and none of the site's existing anti-adblock rules stops it. Three candidate rules (two scriptlets and one HTML-filtering rule) produced no change in any experiment phase while the experiment's own probe reported no anti-adblock detected and no applied rules, so no candidate could be verified and the best scriptlet candidate is handed over for human review.

## Candidate for review

`jpopsingles.eu#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-stack-trace', 'requestAnimationFrame', 'js_func_frame_loop')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: All three experiments came back environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with empty failedCandidateChecks, and the vision review rejected each as 'symptom:⁠ not_resolved' with pageIntegrity intact and no observedDamage. The record contradicts what it captured:⁠ phase A reported an empty appliedRules list although the run's own session lists 21 applied rules on the same page, phase C reported antiAdblockDetected:⁠false although that phase's screenshots show the banner, and two candidates produced byte-identical before/after full-page captures. That points to the candidate not being applied by the adapter's filtering engine rather than to a proven failure of the rule, so it stayed browser-unverified. The mechanism it targets is evidenced separately:⁠ only the detector's inline script uses requestAnimationFrame on this page, and js_func_frame_loop stayed stable across two loads while all other identifiers were randomized.

## Still visible after the rule

- Top center above the post grid, overlapping site header/navigation and first post cards — Visible anti-adblock overlay:⁠ red 'AdBlock Detected' header with white message box 'Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us.' over a dark translucent blackout layer. The site logo, navigation, first post cards ([⁠Single]⁠ PIGMONZ – G.M.B.A and [⁠Single]⁠ ZARAME – Kodou), sidebar Info/Donate area, and Recent Posts are dimmed behind it.
- Top center, overlapping the site header/navigation above the post grid — Prominent anti-adblock banner:⁠ red header reads "AdBlock Detected" and a white box reads "Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us."; the reporter circled this banner in red.
- Full page behind the banner, including header, navigation, post cards and right sidebar — Dark blackout/dim overlay covers the page content beneath the anti-adblock banner, matching the gated/dimmed page state described by the reporter.

## Missing information

- Scriptlet argument semantics (abort-on-stack-trace / abort-current-inline-script) and HTML-filtering support in AdGuard CLI are not covered by the run's guidance documents: The run's three linked documents (create-own-filters.md, filter-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) served via lookup_rule_guidance give the #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet rule syntax and the $$ HTML-filtering syntax with :⁠contains(), but not the per-scriptlet argument semantics of the Scriptlets library (what abort-current-inline-script's property/searchString actually match against, and what abort-on-stack-trace matches in a stack frame), nor which of scriptlets/HTML filtering the AdGuard CLI adapter actually applies. I needed both:⁠ the candidate had to abort an inline detector that only touches the trapped property from inside a load-event callback, and no document states whether HTML filtering rules are executed by the CLI product or by the experiment adapter.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40147001729

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance is the first-party cookie consent banner ("We value your privacy") on www⁠.ipqualityscore.com, rendered into the shadow root of div#⁠ipqs-consent by /templates/js/consent.js. Adding the domain-scoped element-hiding rule ipqualityscore.com#⁠#⁠#⁠ipqs-consent to the Cookie Notices filter removed the banner in the verified A/B/C experiment with the page intact. ## Rule `ipqualityscore.com###ipqs-consent` ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ the report is an annoyance cookie notice, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so no policy rule closes it or hands it to a maintainer. Filter-policy guidance assigns cookie notices and CMPs to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter and states that hiding or blocking the notice is the usual sufficient method. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40151938372 Automated analysis against filters at `f404d01`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZW0tKX_iFhc&t=109s](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DZW0tKX_iFhc%26t%3D109s) ### Comment > ## Summary > > YouTube AI auto-dubbed audio tracks disappear when AdGuard for Windows filters HTTPS traffic for `youtube.com`. Adding only `youtube.com` to the HTTPS allowlist brings them back. No filtering rule seems to be involved. > > ## Screenshots (UI is in Portuguese, translation below) > > Both screenshots show the same video, in the same browser, a few seconds apart. The only change is the AdGuard protection toggle. > > **Screenshot 1 - AdGuard ON (dubbing missing)** > > - AdGuard window: "A protecao esta ativada" = "Protection is enabled" > - YouTube player settings menu: > - Volume estavel = Stable volume: **available, ON** > - Iluminacao cinematografica = Ambient mode: ON > - **Faixa de audio = Audio track: MISSING** > - Legendas/CC = Subtitles/CC: Off > - Timer de suspensao = Sleep timer: Off > - Velocidade da reproducao = Playback speed: Normal > - Qualidade = Quality: Auto (720p60) > > **Screenshot 2 - AdGuard OFF (dubbing works)** > > - AdGuard window: "A protecao esta desativada" = "Protection is disabled" > - YouTube player settings menu: > - Volume estavel = Stable volume: **greyed out (unavailable)** > - Iluminacao cinematografica = Ambient mode: ON > - **Faixa de audio = Audio track: Portuguese (BR)** > - Legendas/CC = Subtitles/CC: Off > - Timer de suspensao = Sleep timer: Off > - Velocidade da reproducao = Playback speed: Normal > - Qualidade = Quality: Auto (1080p60 HD) > > Note that it's not only the audio track. Stable volume also flips between the two states, which makes me think YouTube is sending a different player configuration when AdGuard is in the middle, rather than something just being hidden on the page. > > ## Environment > > - AdGuard for Windows 8.0.3 (build 8.0.5587), Windows 11 (26H2) > - Browser: Chromium-based (identifies as Chrome 156) > - Test video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZW0tKX_iFhc > - No user rules > > ## Steps to reproduce > > 1. Keep HTTPS filtering enabled (default settings). > 2. Open the test video and open the player settings (gear icon). > 3. Result: no "Audio track" option. > 4. Add `youtube.com` to Settings > HTTPS filtering > Website allowlist, restart the browser, reload the video. > 5. Result: "Audio track" is back with the dubbed languages. > 6. Remove `youtube.com` from the allowlist again: the option disappears again. > > ## Expected vs actual > > - Expected: the "Audio track" menu with dubbed languages is shown, the same as on mobile or with AdGuard off. > - Actual: with youtube.com HTTPS-filtered, the menu is missing and the player stays in the original language. > > ## What I already ruled out > > Each of these was tested on its own, and none of them brought dubbing back: > > - **DNS filters:** with only DNS protection active, dubbing works. The DNS lists (AdGuard DNS filter, YousList) don't block anything the player needs. > - **Full allowlist rule** `@@||www.youtube.com^$important,document`: still broken. > - **All JS/scriptlet rules off on YouTube** with the user rule `@@||youtube.com^$jsinject`: still broken. > - **Tracking protection (Stealth mode) fully off:** still broken. > - **Annoyances filter and AI-related filters off:** still broken. > - **AdGuard browser extension off:** no change, since the app filters the browser. > - **Other domains:** `googlevideo.com`, `ytimg.com` and `ggpht.com` don't need to be excluded. Only `youtube.com` matters. > - **Filter lists and log:** I went through the YouTube rules in the Base filter and the filtering log. Nothing touches the audio tracks, and the `/youtubei/v1/player` request isn't blocked or rewritten by any rule. > > ## Workaround and its cost > > Putting `youtube.com` in the HTTPS allowlist (or turning HTTPS filtering off) fixes dubbing, but in-video YouTube ads come back, since the app can no longer filter that traffic. > > ## Timeline > > - Until about a week ago, I could pause filtering, select the dubbed track and turn filtering back on, and it would keep working. > - About a week ago, the audio menu started showing only the original language. > - After updating to 8.0.3 (October 22, 2026), the audio menu disappeared completely and the old trick stopped working: the player falls back to the original language on reload. > > ## My guess > > Since no rule seems to be involved, I suspect the HTTPS interception itself. With AdGuard proxying the connection, YouTube sees a browser that claims to be Chrome (user agent and `x-browser-validation` header) but has AdGuard's TLS/HTTP fingerprint. YouTube may treat that as an unverified client and serve a reduced player without experimental features such as AI dubbing. > > Someone else on the same AdGuard version doesn't have this issue, so YouTube experiment groups may play a part too. > > I can send filtering log exports (with and without the exclusion) if that helps. ### Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"da296cf3c5dcd0c935f7278251565eb3d4e63f382b10abb4f8aa2ba0ebf37656"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The Guardian's "Disable Your Adblocker" wall could not be reproduced:⁠ the reported homepage, the exact screenshot article and two other articles loaded through the AdGuard CLI proxy baseline showed no anti-adblock markup after waiting and scrolling, and the captured requests contain no detector script that renders such a wall. Under the run instruction's anti-adblock rule this goes to a maintainer rather than getting a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The wall is not a German site's wall, and the captured request inventory contains no detector script that renders it, so the gate for writing a rule is not met. Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." The absence of the wall in this environment is an observation for a maintainer, not a decision this run may make. No rule family could be extended instead:⁠ the only site-level anti-adblock selectors already present (`.adblock-sticky__message`, `.js-adblock-sticky`) describe a different, sticky message, and the anti-adblock bait is already excepted by `theguardian.com#@#.ad_unit`.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40162828474

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `f404d01`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — speedof.me's reported ads are Ad-Shield ad-recovery units (two rail cards plus an "AD"-labelled floating card over the results chart) served from the site's own bundle, and no element-hiding rule both removes them and keeps the results page intact:⁠ hiding the containers makes the platform re-render ads (once inside the results container), while safer selectors leave re-rendered rail ads. Three apply_rule experiments were run and all were rejected (one with page damage, two with remaining instances), so this is reported analysis-only for human review of a scriptlet-level fix.

## Still visible after the rule

- Left rail beside the results chart, x≈0–160, y≈147–742 — Tall dark rounded promo/ad card reading 'Let Claude run the speed test' with code icon, 'WORKS WITH AI AGENTS' label, body text, and yellow 'See MCP server' button. Visible advertising/promo card in the reporter-defined rail location.
- Right rail beside the results chart, x≈1757–1919, y≈147–742 — Tall white rounded promo/ad card reading 'Run this test from your own code' with developer code snippet and yellow 'See the API' button. Visible advertising/promo card in the reporter-defined rail location.

## Missing information

- No guidance for third-party ad-recovery (Ad-Shield) slots that re-inject ads and also carry house creatives: speedof.me serves its ads through the Ad-Shield ad-recovery platform bundled first-party (speedof.me/api/core.js, no third-party ad host in the HAR). The run instruction and the linked policy documents cover first-party ads, German anti-adblock walls, and anti-adblock walls "once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script", but they say nothing about (a) a third-party ad-recovery slot that alternately serves third-party creatives and the site's own promo creatives, and (b) the platform's re-injection behaviour:⁠ when the ad containers are hidden, apply_rule's AFTER phases showed a new ad unit rendered inside the speed-test results container (#⁠progress_container), and after that was also covered, two new rail units were rendered in the same slots. Guidance on whether such a slot counts as "the site's own advertising" (no rule) or as third-party advertising (rule), and on whether an element-hiding rule is acceptable when the platform re-renders, is missing.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On esports.ru the reporter's marked ads are mostly the site's own tournament/editorial promotion (no rule under policy), but the bottom slot is a third-party Melbet gambling banner the page itself labels "Реклама 18+" and links to tracker.partnersmelbet.ru. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on that affiliate link verified in the before/after experiment:⁠ the banner is gone, no layout residue, page integrity intact. ## Rule `esports.ru##section[data-name="container/section"]:has(a[href^="https://tracker.partnersmelbet.ru/"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a website-filtering ads report; no rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes it:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page. The proposed rule targets third-party paid advertising (Melbet banner with an affiliate tracker link, labelled 'Реклама 18+' by the page), not the site's own advertising:⁠ the site's self-promotion (ESPORTS.RU x FASTCUP tournament creatives and its own editorial figure) is deliberately left in place, as the policy requires. The only third-party scripts observed (mc.yandex.ru/metrika, top-fwz1.mail.ru) are already blocked by the tracking baseline, and no anti-adblock detector request was captured, so no anti-adblock rule is at stake. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 828](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L828). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported nikvesti.com "РЕКЛАМА" sponsored-card block could not be reproduced:⁠ the reported URL returned HTTP 403 in all three browser sessions of the locked adguard_cli environment, so no DOM or network evidence exists to decide whether the block is first-party or vendor-served. One unverified candidate is carried for human review — a case-insensitive variant of the site's existing label rule in CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt.

## Candidate for review

`nikvesti.com#?#.important-news-block:has(> div.important-title:contains(/реклама/i))`

CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: The reported page was never reachable:⁠ the main document returned HTTP 403 in three materially different sessions (mobile ru-RU/untouched, desktop ru-RU/accept, desktop en-US/reject) and the host reported technical_attempt_budget_exhausted, so no DOM, network inventory or applied-rule data existed and apply_rule was never run. The candidate is inferred only from the reporter screenshot (block with a 'РЕКЛАМА' label bar directly above a 2x2 sponsored-card grid) and from the site's existing rule family in the same file (line 2191 `nikvesti.com#?#.important-news-block:has(> div.important-title:contains(Реклама))`; line 2233 mgid-based rule). The container class, label element and vendor are unconfirmed, and whether :⁠contains() is already case-insensitive (making this a duplicate) could not be checked. Also worth inspecting after a page load:⁠ the shared rule `od-news.com,varta1.com.ua##.MIXADVERT_NET` (UkrainianFilter line 691).

## Missing information

- No run route for a reported URL that is blocked (HTTP 403) in every session: The trusted reported URL (nikvesti.com article) returned HTTP 403 on the main document in all three materially different browser sessions of the locked adguard_cli environment; navigation is now exhausted and the host directs an analysis-only finish. The run instruction and the filter-policy document give no branch for this situation:⁠ the report is a T:⁠ Ads report, but without DOM or network evidence the first-party vs third-party nature of the annotated 'РЕКЛАМА' block cannot be established, so neither the "site's own advertising" close branch nor a rule can be grounded. Guidance on how to classify and finish a report whose page is unreachable in the prepared environment would be needed.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported blank area on eurointegration.com.ua is an empty Google AdSense slot container that keeps its reserved height (375px mid-article, 280px below the tag list); hiding those wrappers removes all reserved ad height (12 containers measured 0×0, 14 blank blocks before vs 0 after) with page integrity intact, but the vision review kept rejecting the candidate because it read the site's own \~130px article-separator spacing as leftover ad space, so the rule is carried unverified.

## Candidate for review

`eurointegration.com.ua##div:has(> ins[data-ad-client])`

CyrillicFilters/UkrainianFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: visualReview verdict 'rejected' (symptom 'not_resolved', adLayoutResidue 'present') with pageIntegrity 'intact' and observedDamage empty in all three runs of the candidate. The candidate itself measured clean:⁠ phase B matched 12 AdSense wrappers (6 × 375px + 6 × 280px) and phase C measured every one at 0×0, and a document-wide domCheck counted 14 empty reserved-height blocks before the fix versus 0 after. The review's remaining instances are all the same region:⁠ \~125–190px of white between an article's tag buttons and the site's own blue '.separator' divider, which my own inspection of its flagged AFTER tiles (9f5ac85f, 9a4e7807, 5e112043, 0d13b105, 9c3038b1) and DOM measurement (139px built from a 19px Facebook-comments placeholder, a 19px link, a 5px '.separator' and container padding) show to be the page's own feed spacing rather than ad-slot height. The experiment therefore stayed inconclusive and no verified verdict was reachable within the three runs this candidate gets.

## Still visible after the rule

- Below the article tag list (ФРАНЦІЯ / ПРОТЕСТИ), above the double divider and next article heading 'В Албанії поліція...' — A visibly large empty white reserved area starts immediately below the article tag list and extends to the double divider before the next article heading. No ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is visible in the gap; it is only blank reserved space.
- After tag list АЛБАНІЯ ПРОТЕСТИ, before divider and heading «В Альбанії поліція» — Large empty white reserved ad area below the article tag list; no ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is visible, leaving a tall blank gap before the next article divider.
- After tag list АЛБАНІЯ ПРОТЕСТИ, before divider and heading «Мерц відкинув розмови...» — Large empty white reserved ad area below the next article's tag list; the empty AdSense slot leaves a tall blank gap with no creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder visible before the divider.
- TILE 10 — Document y=5868..6680, below the article tag list (ФРІДРІХ МЕРЦ / УЛЬТРАПРАВІ) and above the section divider — Large empty white reserved advertising gap below the article's tag list. No ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is rendered in the gap, leaving a visibly large blank area where an ad slot reserved space.
- TILE 12 — Document y=7172..7984, below the next article's tag list (США / ВІЙНА З РФ) — Large empty white reserved advertising gap below the article's tag list. No ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is rendered in the gap, repeating the same blank reserved ad-space symptom.
- and 2 more of the same, in the run artifacts

No rule of the run instruction's policy blocks this report:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall; subscription/promo widgets on this site are an accepted annoyance category and the repository already keeps such rules for thecode.media, so rule generation was permitted. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on www⁠.vlast.is is the full-width "Read distraction-free on Substack" app-install banner above the article headline, which the enabled Annoyances/Mobile App Banners filter leaves visible (no repository rule covers vlast.is). The text-anchored rule `vlast.is#?#button:contains(Read distraction-free)` was verified by the before/after experiment:⁠ banner gone, page integrity intact, no residue. ## Rule `vlast.is#?#button:contains(Read distraction-free)` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile app-install banner annoyance, which the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter exists to block; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall. The banner sits in the post content above the headline, not in the site header or menu, so the header/menu exception for Mobile App Banners does not cover it; it spans the full content width and is the first thing shown above the article. No policy rule closes the report and no rule in the repository covers vlast.is, so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On kettanaito.com's blog post the reporter's "subscription, donation" annoyances are the site owner's "Stay in touch" Twitter-follow card and the "Liked my writing? Buy me a coffee!" bar, both served in the page HTML with no request behind them. One domain-scoped, content-anchored element-hiding rule hides both; it verified in the filtering proxy with page integrity intact and no layout residue (DOM checks show the remaining space is the page's own two 80px section margins). ## Rule `kettanaito.com##aside:has(a[href*="twitter.com/intent/follow"]), aside:has(a[href*="buymeacoffee.com"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a website-filtering annoyance (in-page subscription/follow prompt and donation bar), not a product bug, so rule generation is open. None of the run instruction's close rules applies:⁠ these are not the site's third-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (no detector request appears in the captured network log; pageObstruction was none and no anti-adblock was detected). The repository's policy document places self-promotion of a site owner in the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter ("Block self-promotion of websites ... if it is considered an annoying element") and lists donations among Widgets-filter widgets, with the block decision made by filter developers rule-by-rule; the repository already carries donation-widget hiding rules (suntimes.com#⁠#⁠.donate and prosleduetmedia.com#⁠#⁠.donate in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, stopcor.org,roskomsvoboda.org#⁠#⁠.donate in AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt), so this is a proposal for developer judgement rather than a blocked report. Policy caveat recorded for the reviewer:⁠ the Widgets-filter text says donation widgets are not blocked except when they occupy a significant portion of the page and stand out, and Social-filter text says links to a site's own social pages are not blocked; both reported elements are small, so their inclusion is exactly the rule-by-rule decision the policy assigns to maintainers. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Reproduced it:⁠ reshade.me's Redim CookieHint dialog is hidden by the Cookie Notices filter while the plugin still marks #⁠g-page-surround inert, so nothing on the page is clickable (unfiltered, the dialog is visible and "Accept all" restores clicks). The one-rule fix (scriptlet removing `inert`) was applied in phase C but the vision review cannot observe clickability and reported the symptom unresolved, so it cannot be carried; the maintainer-precedent alternative needs two `#@#` exceptions, which a single-rule outcome cannot express.

## Still visible after the rule

- Top navigation bar (Home, Forum, Wiki, Discord, Presets, Guides) — The navigation controls render normally but are part of the inert page container, so they cannot be clicked; no consent dialog is shown that would explain or lift the inert state.
- Hero section — purple 'Download' button below 'Advanced postprocessing everywhere.' — The hero Download button is fully drawn but non-functional:⁠ the page is inert and no consent overlay is present to be accepted, so the control visibly fails to respond.
- Footer — 'Site Notice' and 'Privacy Policy' links next to '© 2014 - 2026 ReShade' — Footer links are rendered but non-interactive for the same reason:⁠ the container remains inert while the consent dialog that would normally remove it is missing from the page.
- Viewport centre / hero region — location where the ReShade consent dialog should appear — The Redim CookieHint consent dialog (logo, 'ReShade asks for your consent…' heading, partner text, 'Manage options' and 'Consent' buttons, close X) is entirely absent, leaving no visible gating content while the underlying page stays inert and unusable.
- Header navigation, Home link — Visible top-nav link; reporter reports it is non-responsive because #⁠g-page-surround remains inert while the consent dialog is hidden.
- and 8 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On anikototv.to the watch page injects a PrivadoVPN banner into the top of the right sidebar (div#⁠networkloop-ad, 300x250 creative from anchoreth.com) via the third-party script https:⁠//cdn.kotocdn.site/ad.js?v=2. The domain-scoped rule ||cdn.kotocdn.site/ad.js$domain=anikototv.to was verified in the reporter profile:⁠ the banner is gone, no reserved gap is left and the page stays intact. ## Rule `||cdn.kotocdn.site/ad.js$domain=anikototv.to` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The banner is a third-party advertiser creative (PrivadoVPN, rel="sponsored") delivered from anchoreth.com through the third-party loader cdn.kotocdn.site/ad.js, not the site's own first-party advertising, so the 'first-party ads:⁠ no rule' policy line does not apply. The report is an Ads report, not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no wall, popup or gate appeared and antiAdblockDetected was false in every validation phase, so neither the German nor the general anti-adblock rule applies. No paywall, scam/phishing or malware element was observed. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40179526355 Automated analysis against filters at `f404d01`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On navalny.com the photo lightbox stayed hidden because the cookie-banner hiding rule `navalny.com##body > div.fixed.z-modal` also matched the gallery's two full-screen `div.fixed.inset-0.z-modal` overlays. The site-pinned exception `navalny.com#@#body > div.fixed.z-modal` was verified:⁠ before it no preview opened, after it the enlarged photo with pagination dots opens and the page stays intact with no ads, though the cookie notice returns. ## Rule `navalny.com#@#body > div.fixed.z-modal` ## Policy rationale The report is a false positive (T:⁠ Incorrect Blocking) about first-party page functionality, not an anti-adblock wall, paywall or the site's own advertising, so no policy rule closes it. The rule is a site-pinned exception that restores a legitimate first-party photo viewer and unblocks no advertising or tracker. The run's candidate preference puts a narrowly scoped, site-pinned cosmetic exception first; the verified candidate follows it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_allowlist.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f404d017ca1d47ff8b1bf0c3dd41b9c258b3ca7a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_allowlist.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ac89cc4dc42d83c1195a1722c6aa893dc1cacd833aaf6a3012dee281a5d4409d"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The banner reported on www⁠.diariocoimbra.pt is the publisher's own first-party ad carousel (div.slider-publicidade filled with self-hosted /wp-content/uploads/…/Pub-dc-*.webp creatives); the page issues no third-party ad requests at all, so filter policy's "site's own advertising — no rule; recommend closing" applies and no rule is proposed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." KnowledgeBase filter policy (ad blocking filters, limitations and exceptions):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked." The reported banner is the publisher's own first-party-served ad inventory:⁠ its creatives are publisher-uploaded images under https:⁠//www⁠.diariocoimbra.pt/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Pub-dc-*.webp inside div.swiper-container.slider-publicidade, and the 154-request HAR of the loaded page contains no ad-network or ad-server host at all, so any rule would deliberately block the site's own advertising rather than a third-party ad request. The agent does not close the issue; this is a recommendation for a maintainer to check.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40182090256

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"f366fc073440e262b737a66746ccf62f6ab233910ceff9e017cef77ba20175d7"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported 2x2 sponsored casino banner grid on v2.ohli365.org reproduces live (full-page vision:⁠ symptom present) and is served first-party from the site's own /api/banner-image/ endpoint inside aside[⁠data-ad-slot]⁠ elements, so I proposed v2.ohli365.org#⁠#⁠aside[⁠data-ad-slot]⁠ for BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt. apply_rule removed every banner with no residue or remaining instances, but the vision review rejected it for page-integrity "damage" in lower sections that my baseline session shows are the site's own pre-existing loading placeholders, so the candidate stays browser-unverified and the run ends analysis-only.

## Missing information

- Policy line "The site's own advertising (first-party ads)" does not define first-party-delivered third-party ads: The run instruction's filter policy says "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing", and the linked filter-policy document says "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked". Neither document states whether an ad served from the reported site's own host and HTML (here:⁠ `aside[data-ad-slot]` elements wrapping casino creatives fetched from the site's own `/api/banner-image/<uuid>.png`) counts as "the site's own advertising" when the advertised brands are third parties (shobu.casino, zxc.bet, dal.bet, add.bet, marked rel="sponsored"), or whether only self-promotion of the site's own products falls under the exception. The run needed that distinction to decide between a rule and a policy-blocked close, and resolved it as "self-promotion only" on the strength of the same document listing "Banners — advertisements displayed as images in various parts of web pages" as a blockable goal.

## Artifacts

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"f755b2616a00d94db34491e3879224b8c18281e2b42d49367568d61a133ce9bb"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reporter's screenshots show ligainsider.de's own German anti-adblock wall ("Adblocker erkannt", instructions to switch the ad blocker off for ligainsider.de), and on the current filtered baseline the page loads normally with the German filter's existing ligainsider.de anti-adblock scriptlets active. Per the run instruction's policy, German anti-adblock walls get no rule, so this is recommended for closing by a maintainer.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site." The page in the reporter's own screenshot 1 is exactly that:⁠ a German-language wall headed "Adblocker erkannt" that explains the site is financed by advertising and instructs the visitor to "Schalte deinen Adblocker für ligainsider.de aus und lies wie gewohnt kostenlos weiter", with a "So schaltest du den Adblocker aus" how-to and a paid ad-free Plus alternative. It detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it on a German site. The reporter's choice of the "Incorrect Blocking" type and the "T:⁠ Incorrect Blocking" label are report metadata, not evidence of what the page shows; the page content itself is the anti-adblock wall, so the German-wall policy applies. Because a repository policy rule forbids generating a rule for this case, no candidate rule was produced; the decision goes to a maintainer, who checks and decides (the agent never closes an issue).

## Artifacts

The symptom is a Google follow/preferred-source promotion panel in the article's subscribe row; the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter purpose explicitly covers blocking annoying self-promotion of websites, and the Popups/Subscriptions section already carries this site's neighbouring subscription-promo rules. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfe78dfa12fa9968eeaa8d22d3d38446d11ba95a/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.gate02.ne.jp the reporter's boxed annoyance block is the "このページをシェアする" share row plus the pale lavender Google "preferred source" prompt panel; both are baked into the served HTML and neither is caught by existing rules. A content-anchored element-hiding rule scoped to gate02.ne.jp removed both (265px of clutter) in the verified before/after experiment with no page damage. ## Rule `gate02.ne.jp##div:has(> a[href^="https://www.google.com/preferences/source"]), div:has(> div > a[href*="x.com/share"])` ## Policy rationale The report is neither the site's own advertising, a paywall, nor an anti-adblock wall; it is a promotional/annoyance block, so no policy rule closes it. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — reviews.konsumentenecho.de shows a fixed full-width cookie-consent bar ("Wir verwenden Cookies …" with an OK button) rendered by the site's own scripts, which no existing filter rule hides. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on the consent widget's stable confirm-button id was verified in the AdGuard Browser Extension:⁠ the bar was visible on the baseline page and hidden with the rule applied, page integrity intact. ## Rule `reviews.konsumentenecho.de##body > div:has(#rcc-confirm-button)` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported symptom is a cookie-consent notice, not the site's own advertising, a paywall, or a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The page's captured requests show no anti-adblock detector script; the captured hosts are the site itself plus googletagmanager.com, bat.bing.com and google.com/doubleclick, and the banner is rendered by the site's own bundle, so the anti-adblock hand-off rule does not apply. No existing rule in the repository covers this site or this consent widget, so a new domain-scoped rule is needed rather than an extension of a shared rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfe78dfa12fa9968eeaa8d22d3d38446d11ba95a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — follow.yahoo.co.jp's large red Yahoo! JAPAN app-install promotion block (banner, store-badge row and fine print, \~533px) still appears because the repository's existing rule for it matches only the old class naming; a selector anchored on the component's current class name hides the whole block with page integrity intact. ## Rule `follow.yahoo.co.jp##div[class*="__AppPromotion"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's policy list does not block this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not a first-party ad-inventory placement — it is an app-install promotion banner, the category the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter exists for ('blocks banners and popups that encourage visitors to install mobile apps'). Filter-policy limitation checked:⁠ the banner is neither a non-animated header/menu banner nor a footer banner; it is a 533px standalone promotion block on a 3331px page, i.e. a significant portion of the usable space. The repository already carried a rule for this exact element on this exact domain (AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt:⁠748) that the site's class rename made dead, so the proposal restores existing scope instead of widening it. Declared signals (AdGuard for iOS product, T:⁠ Annoyance label) were treated as evidence only; the environment was chosen from where the reported product executes filtering. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfe78dfa12fa9968eeaa8d22d3d38446d11ba95a/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — antispyshop.de still shows the iubenda consent overlay "Cookie-Einwilligung verwalten" with the repo baseline, because the shared cookie rule for `body #iubenda-cs-banner` does not list this domain. Adding the reported domain to that existing shared element-hiding rule was verified in the extension A/B:⁠ the banner is gone and the page stays intact. ## Rule `antispyshop.de##body #iubenda-cs-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent banner annoyance (issue comment "Cookie banner"; the page shows the iubenda dialog "Cookie-Einwilligung verwalten"), which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle — no policy rule closes it. It is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the dialog only asks for a cookie decision (Zustimmen / Ablehnen / Einstellungen anzeigen) and contains no ad-blocker detection or disable-your-blocker wording, so the run instruction's 'recommend closing' cases do not apply. Hiding the banner is sufficient per the maintainer rules:⁠ after the candidate was applied the page content stayed visible and usable, so no scriptlet or detector neutralization is needed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfe78dfa12fa9968eeaa8d22d3d38446d11ba95a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 292](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dfe78dfa12fa9968eeaa8d22d3d38446d11ba95a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L292). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40201916988 Automated analysis against filters at `dfe78df`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"fee16844fbbc3e7a6f7ea206c9b78875054bdd65b8e36e0e4e13ceb6ec06933b"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — With the reporter's own filter selection applied, the reported Crunchyroll /ko/ consent layers (Korean terms-update banner and cookie sheet) never rendered:⁠ two structured full-page inspections and DOM checks found no such overlay while the page loaded and displayed normally, so the defect could not be reproduced. Absence is partly filter-caused (the existing trusted-set-cookie scriptlet for anonymous_consent_tos and the existing OneTrust block), and no element was ever visible to anchor a rule on, so no new rule is proposed.

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not a non-anti-adblock scam page, and no anti-adblock wall was observed at all. Rule generation is therefore allowed; the close recommendation rests on reproduction, not on a policy block.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"d9ea860d5815dcb70a894659a0fa79d67e881cb9325340ed391354582980b88c"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

tv.youtube.com shows only its own "use Chrome or Firefox" browser-support notice, and the reported watch page is behind a Google sign-in wall we cannot pass; the captured requests contain no ad-block detector script, so per the run policy the report goes to a maintainer instead of a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' The captured requests on tv.youtube.com contain no ad-block detector script, so the policy blocks rule generation and routes the report to a maintainer. The report is not one of the policy's no-rule cases that would allow recommending a close instead:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall — the label is 'T:⁠ Anti Adblock Script' on an English-language US site. Maintainer rule 'Anti-adblock popups:⁠ hide the popup when that is enough' cannot be applied either:⁠ no popup, wall or overlay with ad-blocker text exists in the reachable page's DOM, so there is no popup to hide and no detector to neutralize.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40204198158

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `dfe78df`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.heizungsfinder.de a DAA/CCM consent panel (#⁠ccm-widget, "WIR NUTZEN COOKIES UND ANDERE TECHNOLOGIEN.") sits fixed over the article; it is a cookie notice, not an anti-adblock wall, and the repo already hides this exact widget id on other sites. It is not the site's own advertising and not a paywall. ## Reproduced symptom

The reported guessthe.game banner advertises "Kinda Hard Golf", which the site itself lists among its own sister sites, so it is the site's own (self-promotion) advertising that repo policy says not to block deliberately; the ad stack behind it (html-load.cc/Ad-Shield, a.pub.network/Freestar) is already blocked by existing Base filter rules and no ad slot renders on the live baseline page. Recommend closing with no rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The only ad creative evidenced in the report is a banner promoting 'Kinda Hard Golf' (kindahardgolf.com), which the reported site itself lists under 'Check out our sister sites:⁠' — the publisher's own property, i.e. the site's own (self-promotion) advertising. Run instruction, Filter policy does not list any other rule that closes this report; the report is not an anti-adblock wall, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock popup, and not a scam/phishing page. AdGuard filter policy (lookup_rule_guidance, policy):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" — so no new rule may be written for this creative, and the generic Base filter rules that already suppress the ad stack must stay as they are.

After restarting the PC, I downloaded the latest installer from the official website and reinstalled it. The installer finished successfully, but the UI still won't open. > * GPU Hardware Acceleration Test: Suspecting a display conflict, I tried executing the command with the GPU bypass flag: "C:\Program Files\AdGuard\AdGuard.exe" /disable-gpu, but the interface still failed to render. > * Graphics Drivers Cleanup: I performed a completely clean installation of the official NVIDIA graphics drivers for the GTX 970 using the "Perform a clean installation" option to wipe any leftover registry paths or driver traces from the RTX 4090. The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

adblockeraio.pro/aio.php serves no advertising at all:⁠ it is a single-purpose first-party landing page promoting the operator's own "All-In-One Adblocker" Chrome extension, identical with and without filtering. Per the run instruction's policy ("The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing"), no rule is needed — recommend closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported page serves only the operator's own promotion card for its own 'All-In-One Adblocker' Chrome extension — no third-party ad request exists in the HAR and the baseline applied 0 rules. No ad-serving element or empty ad placeholder exists to hide:⁠ inspect_ad_slots reported 0 candidates and the unfiltered control session shows the same card, so a cosmetic rule would only blank the page's sole content and a whole-domain block would deliberately block the site's own advertising, which the policy forbids. The only third-party request on the page (static.cloudflareinsights.com beacon) is already covered by the existing shared rule ||static.cloudflareinsights.com^ in SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers_firstparty.txt, so no new rule is needed for it. No anti-adblock wall is present:⁠ the page does not detect the ad blocker, and the only extension check is for the site's own extension ID, so the anti-adblock and German-wall provisions do not apply.

## Artifacts

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ade77a3616e1f0fbc3c41651e59793148655c943fc5f5f3b68cc1d4970dccb5a"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reporter's target — the right-hand "Partners" rail on tanstack.com's docs page — is the site's own first-party sponsored-placement advertising (first-party scripts and SVG logos, sponsor links carrying utm_source=tanstack, "Become a Partner" mailto to partners@⁠tanstack.com, no ad network in the HAR), so the repository's policy "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing" applies and no rule is proposed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter-annotated element is exactly that — TanStack's own sponsored-placement rail, served and rendered by tanstack.com itself. Live evidence proves first-party provenance:⁠ the rail is built by first-party scripts (/assets/PartnerRail-CSWHUp0O.js, /assets/PartnersGrid-D9EIrW0.js-equivalent PartnersGrid-D9EIrIWo.js, /assets/usePartnerPlacementContext-yb4Ue46d.js), all sponsor logos are tanstack.com/assets/*.svg, "Become a Partner" is mailto:⁠partners@⁠tanstack.com, and the sponsor links carry the site's own attribution (utm_source=tanstack, utm_medium=sponsor, utm_campaign=gold-launch). No third-party ad or sponsorship vendor appears anywhere in the HAR (artifact:⁠har:⁠a7adc551-521e-4bfb-b155-151b146b4c07):⁠ every host is tanstack.com plus fonts, Sentry, Scarf and one namethathost tracker — so this is not a removable third-party ad loader that could be blocked at network level. AdGuard filter policy (cited by lookup_rule_guidance) states under Ad blocking filters ⁠> Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." Nothing in the baseline blocks this rail, so the exception clause does not apply and no rule may be written. The report does not fall under any other policy branch:⁠ it is not an anti-adblock wall, not a paywall, not a scam/phishing page, and not a gated-function placeholder; the Annoyances categories (cookie notices, popups, mobile app banners, widgets, other annoyances/self-promo) do not cover a site's own paid sponsor rail.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — yudey.com.ua shows a first-party cookie/privacy consent overlay (section#⁠yudey-consent-banner, fixed at the bottom, "Налаштування приватності" with Відмовитися / Дозволити аналітику / Налаштування) that covers page content and is not covered by any existing rule. Adding yudey.com.ua#⁠#⁠#⁠yudey-consent-banner to the Cookie Notices filter was verified in the locked AdGuard CLI route:⁠ the overlay is hidden and page integrity stays intact. ## Rule `yudey.com.ua###yudey-consent-banner` ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes only first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and other anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; this report is a cookie/privacy consent notice, which none of those rules covers. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this symptom (filter-policy:⁠ 'this filter is designed to block both cookie notices and requests from cookie management platforms'), and hiding is sufficient here because no feature or content is gated behind the consent decision. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d0a3c4aba799d1b3718b18cd67232bcd0d02665a/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"890aa209f238cf773f2bfb579eec717a273569ccc8d1dd95f08785a080025035"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported cookie-consent card is absent on the live www⁠.predictwind.com page:⁠ structured full-page vision of the current extension session with the reporter's filters shows zero instances, and an unfiltered control (desktop, after reload, /pricing, mobile) also shows none, with no consent-management request behind it — so no rule can be built or verified.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party ads, paywalls and anti-adblock walls; a cookie notice is none of them, so no policy rule blocks rule generation. No rule is proposed because the reported defect did not reproduce in live evidence, not because policy forbids a rule.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40233001402

Indeterminate — The reported anti-adblock membership modal on www⁠.thegatewaypundit.com did not appear in the locked AdGuard CLI proxy baseline using the reporter's own filter selection:⁠ four successful loads of the reported URL plus one article page, and structured full-page vision of the reported URL, found no modal, no overlay text in the DOM and no obstruction, so no rule was written and the report is recommended for closing as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules do not cover this report:⁠ the site is not German and the reported prompt is a non-German anti-adblock/membership wall, so no 'no rule needed' policy rule applies; the reason for recommending a close is non-reproduction, not a policy block. comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"cebdd5fb26ae87b4c3f76187bebe5ba6dc0bd0a06b5b8e3b1309f1a2bda43375"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

suketiawan.com shows no anti-adblock wall, popup or detector script on the reported page in desktop and mobile filtered sessions (HTTP 200, zero rules applied, no ad/detector host in the HARs), and its only ad inventory is the site's own first-party banner. Per the run instruction, a non-German anti-adblock report gets a rule only when the captured requests show the detector script, so I recommend closing and handing the report to a maintainer.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, filter policy:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' This is an Indonesian site, not a German one, so the German-wall exception does not apply; the captured requests of the reported page contain no ad-blocker detector script (no adblock/blocker/adsbygoogle strings in any inline script, no ad or detector host in the HAR), so the report goes to a maintainer instead of a rule. Run instruction, filter policy:⁠ 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' The only ad-like inventory on the page is the site's own first-party 300x250 banner /wp-content/uploads/2015/07/iklan.gif.webp inside a WordPress custom ad spot linking to wa.me/6285850050637, which is also what the sidebar panel in the issue screenshot shows. Filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md):⁠ 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked'; anti-adblock walls are only blocked when they aggressively insist on disabling the blocker or effectively prevent using the website, and here no wall of any kind was observed.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40236679415

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `d0a3c4a`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — catster.com articles inject a full-screen dimmed "Catster discount"/Chewy "Save 35%" promo modal about 25 seconds after load, and it reproduces with the reporter's filter set; the verified fix is the domain-scoped element-hiding rule `catster.com##div[data-pango-opportunity-id]` in the Popups filter's site-specific section. ## Rule `catster.com##div[data-pango-opportunity-id]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a dismissible promotional popup overlay gating an article, which the AdGuard Popups filter's stated purpose covers ("popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions"; "other types of popups that may annoy users"). It is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an in-content first-party ad slot, so none of the run instruction's no-rule clauses applies. No existing shared rule or vendor family covers the pango opportunity modal, so a new domain-scoped rule is needed. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d0a3c4aba799d1b3718b18cd67232bcd0d02665a/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
